title: Marguerite and the Verdict
premise: Felix Fairweather has spent twelve years as the night dispatcher for Bellhaven Taxi, listening to the town confess itself through fare requests she never repeats. When a letter arrives confessing to the murder of local patriarch Edmund Voss—postmarked the day after his funeral—Felix recognizes the handwriting as her late mother's, who died a year ago. Following the letter's coded references to a taxi ledger her mother once kept, Felix uncovers that Edmund Voss's fortune was built on a hit-and-run her mother witnessed and was paid to forget, and that the Voss heir, Julian, is quietly eliminating everyone who knew. In the end Felix chooses to hand the ledger not to the police but to a journalist, trading her invisibility for a public reckoning that destroys the Voss inheritance and finally lets her mother rest.
about_author: Yara Yarrow is a former small-town court stenographer who spent a decade transcribing other people's worst days before turning them into fiction. She lives in the fog belt of the northern coast, where she keeps meticulous records of everything, including things that never happened.

chapters.title: The Night Shift
chapters.summary: Felix Fairweather, POV. We meet Bellhaven's night dispatcher: forty calls a night, twelve years of secrets alphabetized in her head. She picks up a fare request from Voss Manor and feels an old unease. Beat: the comfort of routine, and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A confession letter arrives admitting to Edmund Voss's murder, dated the day after his funeral. The handwriting stops her cold: it's her dead mother's. Beat: grief reopened, the world tilting off its axis.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with a flashback. She compares the letter to old letters her mother, Ruth, sent from prison—Ruth died inside a year ago for a crime Felix never fully understood. Beat: a daughter's doubt curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: The Voss Funeral Nobody Cried At
chapters.summary: Felix observes Edmund Voss's memorial from the back of the room, driving the late fares home afterward. She catalogs who cried, who didn't. Beat: the town's hypocrisy rendered as a seating chart.

chapters.title: Fare 47
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She finds an entry her mother made decades ago in the company's old paper ledger: a fare from Voss Manor at 2:14 a.m., the night a schoolteacher was killed on Miller's Road. Beat: the first hard evidence that Ruth's letter is a map.

chapters.title: Julian Voss, Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The new master of Voss Manor learns a letter exists and begins quietly asking the dispatcher's coworkers about her. Beat: the predator entering the story, patient and polite.

chapters.title: What Ruth Never Said
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She visits Ruth's old cellmate, now a laundromat owner, who reveals Ruth confessed to protect someone and that 'the ledger is in plain sight.' Beat: maternal love reinterpreted as a burden Ruth chose.

chapters.title: Dispatch
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, night montage. She starts cross-referencing twelve years of fare logs against the ledger codes, working through her shifts. Beat: the thrill of competence, the dispatcher as detective.

chapters.title: The Man Who Pays Cash
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A recurring anonymous fare—always cash, always to the county courthouse—turns out to be the retired officer who worked the hit-and-run case and buried it. Beat: complicity has a face, and it tips well.

chapters.title: Miller's Road at 2:14
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ruth's POV, 1989. The night of the accident: Edmund Voss behind the wheel, Ruth the only witness, and the offer she couldn't refuse because Felix was four years old and hungry. Beat: the price of survival made concrete.

chapters.title: A Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Julian Voss visits the dispatch office, all charm, offering her a 'consulting fee' for any correspondence concerning his father. Beat: fear dressed as generosity; she takes the check to buy time.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She realizes the coded entries map onto the taxi company's own fare zones—the ledger is the wall map in the dispatch office, annotated in her mother's hand. Beat: revelation as homecoming; the secret hung above her for twelve years.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Someone cuts the dispatch office phone line during a storm night; a fare she never ordered waits outside, engine running. Beat: the watcher becomes the watched.

chapters.title: The Retired Officer Talks
chapters.summary: Deputy-turned-private citizen Harlan Boyd's POV. Boyd admits to Felix that he falsified the Miller's Road report for Voss money, and that Ruth's confession to an unrelated crime was the price of her silence. Beat: a coward's confession, half redemption.

chapters.title: Sister of the Deceased
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Edmund's daughter, Camille Voss, approaches Felix—she suspects Julian killed their father over a changed will. Beat: alliances form between the overlooked.

chapters.title: The Changed Will
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. She shows Felix the old will leaving everything to a trust for Miller's Road victims' families, and the new will Julian produced. Beat: inheritance as weapon; the theme sharpens.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She reconstructs her mother's prison visits and realizes Ruth was coaching her all along—every story about fares was a lesson in reading people. Beat: grief transmutes into inheritance of another kind.

chapters.title: The Fare That Never Came
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The night Edmund Voss died, a dispatcher's log shows a canceled pickup from Voss Manor—canceled by someone using Ruth's old account code, dormant for a year. Beat: the letter's postmark date suddenly makes sense.

chapters.title: Someone Used Her Name
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with Boyd. Together they trace the account code: only three people ever knew it. Beat: the suspect pool narrows; paranoia blooms.

chapters.title: Camille's Alibi
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Camille has an airtight alibi for the night Edmund died—too airtight, rehearsed. Beat: trust wobbles; Felix learns everyone lies a little.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She meets Nadia Okafor, an investigative reporter who's been sitting on the Miller's Road file for years, waiting for a source. Beat: the outside-the-law path takes shape.

chapters.title: Threats, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian buys the taxi company's parent corporation and begins dissolution proceedings—Felix will lose her job, her archive, her cover. Beat: the walls close in through paperwork.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Another letter arrives in Ruth's hand, postmarked the day before Edmund's death, warning her to stop. Beat: either Ruth was alive last month, or someone is weaponizing her memory.

chapters.title: Grave Conditions
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She has her mother's grave exhumed quietly via Boyd's contacts: Ruth died exactly when recorded. The letters are forgeries—expert forgeries. Beat: the enemy knows Ruth intimately.

chapters.title: The Third Person in the Cell
chapters.summary: Flashback, Ruth's POV, final prison year. A visitor: a young Julian, learning from Ruth herself the ledger's codes, ostensibly to 'make amends.' Beat: the horror of having taught your blackmailer.

chapters.title: Blackmail, Inherited
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She assembles it: Julian killed his father over the will, then used Ruth's forged letters to frame a dead woman and smoke out the ledger's location. Beat: the full shape of the plot, cold and clear.

chapters.title: Burn Before Reading
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The dispatch office burns—arson timed to the archive's destruction. Felix barely saves the wall map, cutting it from the frame as the sprinklers fall. Beat: sacrifice of the sanctuary; no more hiding.

chapters.title: Out of Service
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, unemployed, hiding at Camille's. She decodes the map's final layer: a safe-deposit key number hidden in the fare grid. Beat: exhaustion and resolve in equal measure.

chapters.title: Boyd's Choice
chapters.summary: Boyd's POV. Julian offers Boyd immunity and money to hand over Felix. Boyd drives to her hiding place—and instead gives her his original 1989 field notes. Beat: a coward finally pays his debt.

chapters.title: The Deposit Box
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The safe-deposit box holds Ruth's true confession, Edmund's signed hush-payment receipts, and a letter to Felix: 'If you're reading this, finish it in daylight.' Beat: maternal blessing as marching orders.

chapters.title: What the Law Can't Touch
chapters.summary: Felix and Nadia's POV, alternating. The statute of limitations has expired on the hit-and-run; the murder of Edmund has no evidence tying Julian but plenty tying the cover-up. Beat: justice outside the law becomes the only road.

chapters.title: The Trap Baited with Truth
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She lets Julian believe she'll sell the ledger, luring him to the dispatch office ruins with a fake meeting. Beat: the invisible woman sets the table.

chapters.title: Fare 47, Return Trip
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, the climax begins. Julian arrives, confesses in the dark believing they're alone—and the taxi he ordered arrives carrying Nadia, a recorder, and Boyd wearing a wire. Beat: the confession, captured.

chapters.title: Miller's Road, Reopened
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Julian, cornered, tries to flee in his own car; Felix, who knows every road's weight limit, has the county already alerted—his escape route is a closed bridge. Beat: her small knowledge defeats his power.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: Courtroom chapter, Felix watching from the gallery as the cover-up, not the killing, convicts: obstruction, conspiracy, fraud. Julian gets decades; the Voss trust is dissolved. Beat: justice arrives sideways, but it arrives.

chapters.title: Restitution
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. The trust is restored; Miller's Road victims' families receive what was stolen from them. Camille and Felix part as something like sisters. Beat: inheritance finally means repair.

chapters.title: Last Call
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The taxi company reopens under new ownership; they offer her the day manager's job. She drives her first fare herself: Harlan Boyd, to the courthouse, to testify in the reopened Miller's Road inquest. Beat: quiet redemption, one ride at a time.

chapters.title: The Letter She Wrote
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She writes to her mother's grave the confession Ruth never got to make publicly, and reads it aloud at the headstone as the fog lifts. Beat: grief resolved into gratitude.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, final chapter. She takes down the alphabetized mental archive, one name at a time, and puts her own name first. The night shift ends; the morning shift begins. Beat: the price of survival paid in full—and worth it.
